articles.title: WWE Raw results, grades (Nov. 23): Roman Reigns and the 946 raise the stakes; Ethan Page retains
articles.summary: The latest "WWE Raw" unveiled the final members for Team USA and Team Mexico, and put some finishing touches on this weekend’s Survivor Series: WarGames matches.
articles.body: "WWE Raw" traveled to Wichita, Kansas on this Monday, Nov. 23, for a special early edition of the show. Tonight's "Raw" unveiled the final members for Team USA and Team Mexico, while further putting the finishing touches on teases for this weekend’s Survivor Series: WarGames matches.Instant actionWWE started tonight’s "Raw" in a very old-school fashion. Instead of showing wrestler arrivals like WWE usually does these days, as soon as the show began, 946 was assaulting Alpha Academy. Those poor dudes can't catch a break.The 946 are on a total TEAR!! 🤯Tozawa and Otis have been DESTROYED!! pic.twitter.com/UqScGTdDWm— WWE (@WWE) November 23, 2026 Michael Cole explained on commentary that Alpha Academy had just finished their match on “WWE Main Event” before they were attacked. The mention was a nice touch, explaining what exactly was going down, and giving that always-fun unpredictability element to the 946’s "Ain't nobody safe" mantra. Then every member got a turn on the mic, punctuated by Royce Keys finally giving some semblance of a verbal explanation of how we got here.It's crazy that it took this long, but better late than never.Nobody is SAFE from The 946! 😤 pic.twitter.com/5QlAeqL7Fx— WWE (@WWE) November 23, 2026 Keys made it clear he intends to take out the Bloodline, then Roman Reigns, securing the World Heavyweight Title in the process. That would be a logical progression, for sure.Reigns was expected to show up tonight, so it boiled down to when — which, of course, was the end of the show. Admittedly, it was a bit of a dud closer for the Survivor Series go-home "Raw" because they just brawled as the show went off air. At the same time, they don't have much else to do at this point until Saturday’s match.WarGames on Saturday is about to go CRAZY!!! 🔥⛓️The Bloodline and 946 will be LOCKED for WAR!! pic.twitter.com/ng4zn9mjl8— WWE (@WWE) November 24, 2026 You know, I say they don't have anything else they could do, but wrestling is an option, of course. It's kind of their job, after all.Throwing until it sticksSeth Rollins is back, and that's a good thing. How we got to it is not.If you watched last Friday's "SmackDown,” you'll have seen just how great everything has been so far with the whole Team USA vs. Team Mexico tag match. It's been genuinely silly in a pretty great way, which feels very weird but refreshing, especially for the stars involved: Cody Rhodes and CM Punk, specifically.The whole concept is circling around those two and their brewing dissension, with Punk anointing himself a team co-captain and Rhodes' slow heel turn. (Hopefully.) So, in a vacuum, Rhodes bringing in Punk's forever rival, Rollins, is brilliant. But if you really think about it, it makes no sense whatsoever and makes almost everyone on Team USA look like an idiot.BURN IT DOWN 🔥 Seth Rollins is the FINAL member of Team USA! @WWERollins pic.twitter.com/23TACTdPoh— WWE (@WWE) November 24, 2026 Sooo... this is awkward 😬@CMPunk | @WWERollins pic.twitter.com/gffAgSk8yh— WWE (@WWE) November 24, 2026 For starters, why would Rollins want to be on a team with Punk in a virtually meaningless match? Not only him, but another rival from the past two years, LA Knight, who in-story has entirely forgotten that he had issues with Punk in the past, too. Even Rhodes! Je'Von Evans is the only one on their team who is just there and cool with everyone.Now, if Rollins' reason is that he just wants to keep annoying Punk for all of eternity, then OK. Did he just want something to do after being left off TV since SummerSlam? Either would be fine and make sense, but at least make it clear. WWE didn't even give the dude mic time tonight, which was a wildly anticlimactic way to end the segment.That's just from one perspective, though. Then you have Rhodes. He knows Punk and Rollins' history, and he blatantly acknowledged it on Friday — up until tonight. He acted like he had no other choice, which is painfully untrue. So, unless he just wanted to be a jerk as payback for Punk's arrogance around the captain status, he willingly made a decision that actually gives his team a worse chance to win. Surely, this also gives WWE a perfect excuse to have Team Mexico win in a scenario where it otherwise would have zero chance.The situation on Team USA has become TENSE to say the least! 🫢 pic.twitter.com/q5BNPq4pBG— WWE (@WWE) November 24, 2026 El Grande returnsEl Grande Americano was revealed as the final member of Team Mexico. It's absolutely incredible when you think about it. The man under the mask belongs to neither country, but currently could have fit on either side for maximum hilarity. Overall, it's just incredible to see Ludwig Kaiser even get this opportunity in a match with all these stars involved. You love to see it.EL GRANDE AMERICANO 🇲🇽Welcome to Team Mexico!! pic.twitter.com/rvLB2nsyGH— WWE (@WWE) November 23, 2026 A missed opportunity for poor Chad Gable getting left out.Breaking down the Vision?Oba Femi essentially still has nothing to do on this show. That's incredibly disappointing in its own right, especially when you hear the reactions this guy generates. But now, Femi has thrown down an ultimatum after being surrounded by The Vision backstage upon his arrival: Stand down or get destroyed."STAND DOWN" ⚠️@Obaofwwe has given The Vision the ultimate warning! pic.twitter.com/33hpkbz2to— WWE (@WWE) November 24, 2026 It feels like an odd route to take, and as much as I want to see every WWE stable outside of the 946 disband, Bron Breakker should be the one to separate from or end The Vision. That, unfortunately, doesn't seem in the cards. That's unless they "stand down" and he disbands them, I suppose.All in all, it's an odd path to take.👑 Uncrowned Gem of the Night 👑Ethan Page and Rey Fenix came out sprinting in their Intercontinental title match. It was a good change of pace for the champion, Page, who retained and reminded fans he can go at a rate like this.The best part of this was Page winning with more "legal cheating." Like, the win wasn't dirty. It was tactfully underhanded, you could say, as Page pulled Fenix's mask to the side, forcing a readjustment. From there, he capitalized and hit his finisher for the win. EGO CHECK ✅@OfficialEGO RETAINS the IC Title! pic.twitter.com/wyfR8OaOvY— WWE (@WWE) November 23, 2026 I mean, this is some really intricate, subtly strong booking for Page. He has been in a great spot since earning his title match.I give Monday's "Raw" a crown score of: 👑 7/10 👑WWE Raw full-card results and match grades:Stephanie Vaquer and Bayley def. Fatal Influence (Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid) — 👑 3.5/5 👑Sol Ruca def. Lyra Valkyria — 👑 3/5 👑Rey Mysterio and El Grande Americano def. The Judgment Day (Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh) — 👑 3.75/5 👑Intercontinental Championship: Ethan Page (c) def. Rey Fenix — 👑 4/5 👑Recap "WWE Raw" with Uncrowned's live blog:

articles.title: Bengals vs. Commanders live updates, inactives, where to watch: Joe Burrow MVP watch continues on 'Monday Night Football'
articles.summary: The Bengals have scored at least 31 points in five straight games. Can they extend the streak to six against the Commanders on "Monday Night Football"?
articles.body: The Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders will close out the Week 11 game slate on "Monday Night Football," with kickoff set for 8:15 p.m. ET at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland.The Commanders defense will have its hands full attempting to contain Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense, which has been on an absolute tear as of late, scoring 31-plus points in each of their past five games. Burrow has emerged as the NFL MVP favorite, leading the league in passing yards per game (310.6), passing touchdowns (27) and completion rate (74.7%) on the way to a 7-2 record and the lead in the AFC North.Though Washington is 3-5-1, its season is far from over. The Commanders are 2.5 games behind the first-place New York Giants in the NFC East, and after a Week 5 tie and a Week 10 win over New York, they hold the head-to-head tiebreaker. A couple of wins down the stretch could put them squarely in the race.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Bengals and Commanders close out Week 11 on "Monday Night Football," airing on ABC and ESPN.

articles.title: Spotify down: Company says outage fixed after 40-minute disruption; users can access accounts and stream music again
articles.summary: Spotify says it has fixed an outage that left tens of thousands of users unable to access the music streaming platform on November 24.
articles.body: Spotify says it has fixed an outage that left tens of thousands of users unable to access the music streaming platform on November 24. The disruption lasted around 40 minutes, with some users reporting that they had been logged out of their accounts and were unable to sign back in. The company has now confirmed that its services are recovering, meaning users should be able to access their libraries and resume streaming music. “Everything’s looking much better now. Thanks for your patience. If you still need help, get in touch at Spotify's status account on X shared the update at 7:08 am ET (5:38 PM IST).What happened during the Spotify outageReports of problems began around 6:29 a.m. ET, according to outage tracker Downdetector. The number of complaints increased over the next few minutes, with users reporting trouble accessing the app and logging into their accounts.Spotify acknowledged the disruption at 6:56 a.m. ET, saying it was aware of the issues and was investigating them.Several users also took to X to report that they had been unexpectedly logged out of their accounts. Some Premium subscribers said they were being asked to create new accounts when they tried to sign in again. Others reported problems receiving login codes through email, making it difficult to regain access.Spotify says services are back, but what caused the outageSpotify has not yet shared what caused Tuesday's disruption. The company has also not provided a detailed explanation of the technical problem behind the login and access issues. Since the outage lasted less than an hour and has now been resolved, it remains unclear whether Spotify will release further details.Users who are still experiencing problems have been asked to report them through Spotify's support channels.Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.
articles.body:
Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The company said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision.

Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the new rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day.

Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.

The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.

The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright . Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services , said that it will introduce a toggle to let users filter out AI music . Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this issue, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures.

Tidal started de-monetizing songs made using AI in June, but that did not prove enough of a deterrent, Tidal Music’s lead, Robert Anderson, said on X.

The company said that 27 million, or 6.3% of tracks on the platform, are fully AI-generated, but 96% of those have no streams.

“It’s true that not all songs catch on immediately, and artists should have time to build their fanbases. But this situation is different – at this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried,” the company said in a post .

Meanwhile, music labels are trying to make money by partnering with platforms and AI model makers to sell their catalog for training or remixing features. Goldman Sachs estimates that by 2035, AI-related licensing tools and new monetization opportunities have the potential to improve record labels’ revenue by 10%.

articles.title: TikTok was down
articles.summary: TikTok is experiencing some issues right now, including problems with videos and search results not loading as expected.
articles.body: Earlier on Tuesday, TikTok experienced some issues, with videos, search results, favorites, and other features not loading as they usually do, following a slew of other outages over the past couple of weeks. Videos sometimes wouldn’t load in the For You feed on my iPhone, and search results occasionally didn’t show up as expected in the app on iOS or Android, or on the web. Even trying to pull up a profile would show a blank page, while links to videos are dead in the water too. However, as of 3:45PM ET or so, things appear to be working normally again. Downdetector showed around 25,000 reports of issues at around 2:56PM ET, and many people on social media were saying that TikTok was down for them. “We experienced a brief technical issue that impacted access to TikTok,” TikTok’s Jessica Casano-Antonellis tells The Verge. “The issue has been resolved. We apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience.” Update, November 24th: Added statement from TikTok.

articles.title: 'Dancing With the Stars' crowns mirror ball winner: Finale recap and latest updates
articles.summary: Paralympian Ezra Frech and pro partner Daniella Karagach won Season 35 of "Dancing With the Stars."
articles.body: Sponsored by EvenityAnd just like that, Dancing With the Stars has crowned its Season 35 winner! Paralympic gold medalist Ezra Frech took home the mirror ball trophy on Tuesday night alongside pro partner Daniella Karagach after they scored a perfect 90/90 on their three performances throughout the evening. At 21 years old, Frech has made history as the youngest-ever mirror ball trophy winner. Frech wasn't the only gold medalist who had a successful evening. Team USA figure skater Amber Glenn and her partner Pasha Pashkov came in second after also scoring 90/90. In third place were Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold, who scored 82/90 during the finale. In fourth place were Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik with 82/90 and in fifth place were Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas, who scored 90/90.The evening featured three rounds of competition and a total of 15 showstopping performances. Glenn's redemptive freestyle performance set to Madonna's "Like a Prayer" and "Music" was one for the books. Frech made a moving statement with his freestyle routine set to Linkin Park's "Numb" — and his quick recovery on the dance floor after his prosthetic leg came off left the judges in awe.Also making a statement tonight was Higgins, who shared a piece of her Irish heritage with audiences. Wood playfully nodded to a beloved Spider-Man actor, while Ali celebrated just how far she's come as a dancer. This season of Dancing With the Stars was one to remember. Read our recap of the Season 35 finale below, and follow for any updates from the stars.

articles.title: Iowa lead detonation live updates: Army blows up toxic explosives despite fears of dust endangering community; 3 states monitoring fallout
articles.summary: The controlled detonation of roughly 5 tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is planned for 9 a.m. local time.
articles.body: The U.S. Army detonated 5 tons of unstable bomb-making chemicals as part of a controlled explosion on Wednesday morning, despite a legal battle over the potential health and environmental impacts from the dust.The explosion detonated the nation's entire stockpile of lead azide, a highly sensitive explosive material, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. The Army has released maps showing where the dust could drift and warned people to avoid the area, adding that children under 6 and pregnant women are particularly vulnerable to lead exposure.The detonation followed an appeals court decision that found adequate safeguards to protect the community were in place. Officials have been taking steps to mitigate the risk, such as barriers around the blast zone.In leaflets handed out to local residents, the Army said the chemicals had degraded, becoming "extremely unstable and sensitive to even slight friction or movement" — meaning there is a risk of an explosion if they attempt to move or store the chemicals any longer. The Environmental Protection Agency said it had granted an emergency permit to detonate 68 drums of the lead azide because a "controlled detonation during optimal weather conditions and incorporating robust mitigation measures, compared to an uncontrolled explosion, significantly reduces the potential reach and concentration of lead dust landing on surfaces, such as homes and windows."Officials in Missouri and Illinois are also monitoring the situation.

images.caption: The U.S. Army detonates a degraded stockpile of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. (Jim Urquhart/Reuters)
People park on the side of the road to watch the Army's detonation of a stockpile of lead azide in Middletown, Iowa, on Wednesday.
A NASA aircraft makes low passes over the Middletown. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)
Journalists prepare to document events while the U.S. Army detonates several tons of highly-volatile, degraded lead azide on the grounds of the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)
Glass is taped to reduce the chance of shattering at a home near the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)
Tarps cover window air-conditioning units at the local post office in Middletown, Iowa. (Austin Johnson/AP)
A home near the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant has its windows taped to prevent shattering. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)
A note taped to a hotel room door warns guests about the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant's planned explosion. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

articles.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed until Saturday due to severe weather — follow live updates
articles.summary: The 100th parade has reportedly been postponed.
articles.body: The annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather — for the first time in history. Officials said Wednesday afternoon that the parade is being postponed until Saturday. “The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” Macy’s said in a statement on Wednesday.A developing nor’easter is expected to bring heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding to the East Coast on Thanksgiving Day. Gov. Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency in neighboring New Jersey on Wednesday. Concerns about whether balloons would be allowed to fly safely mounted as the National Weather Service issued a high wind warning of potentially "strong and damaging wind gusts," expected to start at 10 a.m. on Thursday and continue through early Friday morning. The agency also warned of moderate-to-heavy rainfall.This marks the first time the parade has been postponed due to weather. The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has previously been modified because of weather disruptions. In 1971, all balloons were grounded ahead of the parade due to gusty winds and heavy rainfall. The city also established regulations requiring large balloons to be grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts exceed 34 mph. The regulations were established after an incident during the 1997 parade, in which a Cat in the Hat balloon critically injured a woman after it struck a lamppost.Follow the latest on the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in our blog below.

articles.title: Packers vs. Rams live updates, score: Christian Watson exits after brutal hit from LA safety Kamren Kinchens, who gets ejected
articles.summary: The Packers and Rams kick off Week 11 with a rare Wednesday matchup ahead of Thanksgiving.
articles.body: The Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams will kick off the Week 12 game slate with a Thanksgiving Eve showdown in a rare Wednesday matchup. Kickoff is set for 8:15 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, and the game will air on Netflix.The Packers head into this game with a 6-4 record and would sit as a wild card team if the season ended today in an ultra-competitive NFC North where each team currently sits above.500. They'll get some superstar power back on defense this week, as star defensive end Micah Parsons makes his season debut following an ACL tear suffered last December. The Rams also sit at 6-4 heading into this matchup, but sit just outside the playoff picture, currently three games back from the San Francisco 49ers for the lead in the NFC West. A win on Wednesday night would go a long way toward their playoff hopes — but even if they keep those hopes alive, they'll be moving forward without All-Pro wide receiver Puka Nacua, who is out for the rest of the season with a knee injury.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Packers and Rams kick off Week 11 with a rare Wednesday matchup.
